raw_comment:
I notice that there is a band of severe drought almost in a band horizontally across the country, starting in Wyoming and ending in NJ; also one vertically down the middle of the country. Drought doesn't seem to be connected to a type of geography, save for the fact that Florida has no drought , presumably because it has had such intense storms lately.

I wonder why GA and SC, which also got a ton of rain in the more recent storms are nonetheless abnormally dry. I also wonder why Massachusetts is significantly drier than any of the other New England states, with worse drought conditions seeming to stop at the border of the state. Last, I wonder why there is so much drought and abnormal dryness EVERYWHERE save for just a few pockets. And I could be wrong about this but it looks like drought is worse in sparsely populated places: wyoming, SD, Nebraska, the border of Oklahoma and texas and the texas panhandle. Is that coincidental or relevant?

I'm from massachusetts and so the fact that we are so much drier than our neighbors is concerning. But I also notice that some of the more sever drought is in farming country, and that can't be good. 

Stuck in the Middle With You: From the badlands to the Gulf, the center of the USA is deep in drought
